items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-11-11
items.q: When you go, Kemp go, Allen go, Willie Williams, when you fellas go, goodbye art fellas from New Orleans, no more.

ctx.x: Well, the organizations mostly smaller than they used to be now or about the same size?

Oh, they were big. They had a lot of men belong to them. Yeah, they were very large. Fairlory. I remember when I was a boy, I guess in my middle teens, the art fellas, that's why I tell these art fellas that meet next door here to me, the older fellas like Green and Kemp Jackson and Allen Williams, all them old fellas that was long. You see, my uncle was an art fellow when I was a boy. My uncle belonged to number seven. And as I told you before, they have, they used to have 10th of May where they out. They had a…
I noticed there was a pretty big group in the parade on Saturday. It looked like there were a number of young men in that group.
